title: While Here as Wandering Sheep We Stray
description: While Here as Wandering Sheep We Stray in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 458 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For the Understanding and Influence of God's Word”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: While here as wan-dering sheep we stray, Teach us, O teach us, Lord, thy way! Dis-pose our hearts, with will-ing awe, To love thy word, to keep thy law; That, by thy gui-ding pre-cepts led, Our feet the paths of truth may tread.

lines: While here as wandering sheep we stray,
Teach us, O teach us, Lord, thy way!
Dispose our hearts, with willing awe,
To love thy word, to keep thy law;
That, by thy guiding precepts led,
Our feet the paths of truth may tread.
Great Source of light to all below!
Teach us thy holy will to know:
Teach us to read thy word aright,
And make it our supreme delight;
That, purged from vain desires, our mind
In thee its only good may find.
O hear us when on thee we call!
Preserve us in thy holy ways,
And teach our hearts to speak thy praise!

licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
